01 — The reality today

Information is trapped
in our heads.
Not in the model.

Every deliverable becomes a brand-new job — tendered once, built once, documented twice. The drawings are right. The data lives somewhere else: in spreadsheets, in emails, in people. We decided to fix that at the root.

02 — A fourth era

From drawing by hand to designing with algorithms.

MID
manual
Ink and paper. The drawing is the deliverable.
CAD
1990s
Lines go digital. Faster, but still dumb geometry.
BIM
2010s
The model carries data. Coordination, clash, quantities.
AAD
now
Algorithms-Aided Design. The model designs, checks and renders with you.

Asure builds for the fourth era — where AI is not a plug-in, but the connective tissue between every stage.

REVIT PLUGIN · production

ADS Phoenix L1

A native Revit add-in that runs a fixed 22-point Level-1 self-certification across five hard-stop gates, auto-fixes whitelisted issues, and spits out a PDF report and a populated checklist — in minutes, not a morning.

MCP SERVER · production

Drive Revit
from a chat message.

ads-bridge is a local server that exposes the live Revit session to an AI agent — query the model, run IronPython, set parameters, fire pipelines, grab screenshots. You type; the model moves.

AI STUDIO · production

Idea → photoreal → flythrough.

INFRASTRUCTURE · production

Headroom

Our own context-compression engine sits between the AI and the API, squeezing big, repetitive context — tool outputs, logs, history — before it ever reaches the model. Same answers, a fraction of the tokens.

CHAPTER 03

Philosophy

Why any of this is safe to put in front of a client.
The stance

Not artificial intelligence.
Augmented intelligence.

Every tool keeps an architect at the wheel. AI drafts, checks, renders and compresses — people decide. That's what makes it shippable to real projects with real liability, today.
